title: Indian-American Astronaut Anil Menon Arrives at International Space Station
excerpt: NASA astronaut Anil Menon, the son of an Indian immigrant from Kerala, reached the ISS on July 14 aboard Russia's Soyuz MS-29 spacecraft for an eight-month research mission — his first spaceflight.
body:
• NASA astronaut Anil Menon, 49, launched aboard Soyuz MS-29 on July 14 and docked at the ISS after a three-hour orbital journey — his first spaceflight.
  • Born in Minneapolis to an Indian immigrant father from Kerala and a Ukrainian immigrant mother, Menon is a U.S. Space Force colonel and emergency medicine physician with degrees from Harvard and Stanford.
  • He will spend eight months conducting research on semiconductor crystal production, augmented reality ultrasound, blood flow in microgravity, and bioprinting before returning to Earth in April 2027.
  • NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman traveled to Baikonur Cosmodrome for the launch — the first visit by a NASA chief to Russia's launch facility since 2018.

NASA astronaut Anil Menon and Russian cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina arrived at the International Space Station on July 14, docking at the Prichal module after a three-hour, two-orbit journey from Kazakhstan's Baikonur Cosmodrome. The crew launched aboard Russia's Soyuz MS-29 spacecraft at 10:47 a.m. EDT, increasing the station's complement to 10 for the coming weeks.

The mission marks the first spaceflight for Menon, 49, who was selected for NASA's astronaut corps in 2021 from a pool of more than 12,000 applicants and graduated with the agency's 23rd class in 2024.

From Kerala Roots to Low-Earth Orbit

Menon was born and raised in Minneapolis, Minnesota, to Shankaran Menon, an Indian immigrant from Kerala, and Elizabeth Samoylenko, a Ukrainian immigrant. He is the great-grandson of Chettur Sankaran Nair, according to his Wikipedia biography. After graduating from Saint Paul Academy and Summit School in 1995, Menon earned a bachelor's degree in neurobiology from Harvard University, where he researched Huntington's disease, followed by a master's in mechanical engineering and a medical degree from Stanford University.

"He is the great-grandson of Chettur Sankaran Nair, according to his Wikipedia biography."

A colonel in the U.S. Space Force and practicing emergency medicine physician, Menon's path to orbit traces through some of the most demanding environments on Earth. He deployed to Afghanistan during Operation Enduring Freedom, worked with the Himalayan Rescue Association caring for climbers on Mount Everest, and spent a year in India as a Rotary Ambassadorial Scholar supporting polio vaccination campaigns.

"Selected as a NASA astronaut in 2021, Menon graduated with the 23rd astronaut class in 2024. After completing initial astronaut candidate training, he began preparing for his first space station flight assignment."

— NASA official biography

SpaceX Roots and a Spacefaring Family

Before joining the astronaut corps, Menon served as SpaceX's first flight surgeon, supporting the launch of the company's first crewed Dragon spacecraft during the historic Demo-2 mission in 2020 and building the medical organization to support future human spaceflight. He previously served NASA as a crew flight surgeon for various ISS expeditions.

Menon's wife, Anna Menon, a SpaceX engineer, has already been to space. She flew as a crew member on the Polaris Dawn mission in September 2024, a private astronaut venture commanded by Jared Isaacman — now NASA's administrator. Anna Menon was also part of NASA's September 2025 astronaut class, making the couple one of the few married pairs in the American astronaut corps, according to USA Today.

Eight Months of Research Ahead

During his stint as an Expedition 74/75 crew member, Menon will conduct scientific investigations spanning multiple disciplines, according to NASA. He will continue research to refine in-space production of semiconductor crystals, which could enable large-scale manufacturing of components for high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, and medical devices. He will also perform ultrasound using augmented reality and AI methods aimed at eliminating the need for Earth-based medical support on future deep-space missions.

Menon will serve as a test subject for studies on how blood flow is affected in microgravity — research meant to protect astronauts on longer voyages — and will test bioprinting vascular constructs to advance understanding of the aging process and develop new therapeutics.

A Diplomatic Signal at the Launch Pad

NASA Administrator Isaacman traveled to the Baikonur Cosmodrome for meetings with Roscosmos director Dmitry Bakanov and to watch the launch in person. It was the first visit to Russia's launch facility by a NASA chief since 2018, according to Reuters. Tensions stemming from the Russia-Ukraine war had largely prevented such interactions under former NASA Administrator Bill Nelson during the Biden administration.

The visit signals a potential thaw in U.S.-Russia space cooperation, even as the ISS — a symbol of post-Cold War collaboration — approaches the end of its operational life. The station has hosted more than 280 spacefarers from 26 countries over its 25-plus years in orbit.

Menon, Dubrov, and Kikina are scheduled to return to Earth in April 2027. On the station, they joined NASA astronauts Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway, and Chris Williams, European Space Agency astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud-Sverchkov, Sergei Mikaev, and Andrey Fedyaev.
